samples.summary: New §8.1 claim "Every command that renders a structured result routes it through output()" is not true of the import commands, which the exception list omits

But `docs import`, `notes import` and `slides import` emit structured results with raw `JSON.stringify` and never read `--format`: `packages/cli/src/docs/import.ts:167` `io.stdout(JSON.stringify({ id: replace, replaced: true }, null, 2))`, :215 `io.stdout(JSON.stringify({ id: newId, title: inferredTitle }, null, 2))`, and the same pattern in `packages/cli/src/notes/import.ts:163,217`. finding.summary: New §8.1 claim "Every command that renders a structured result routes it through output()" is not true of the import commands, which the exception list omits
finding.evidence: cli.md:839-845 states every structured-result command routes through `output()`, listing only `login`/`logout`/`ctx switch` (prose) and the *export* file writers as exceptions. But `docs import`, `notes import` and `slides import` emit structured results with raw `JSON.stringify` and never read `--format`: `packages/cli/src/docs/import.ts:167` `io.stdout(JSON.stringify({ id: replace, replaced: true }, null, 2))`, :215 `io.stdout(JSON.stringify({ id: newId, title: inferredTitle }, null, 2))`, and the same pattern in `packages/cli/src/notes/import.ts:163,217`. Grep for `output(` shows no call site in those modules. So `<...> import --format table` silently emits JSON, contradicting the contract this diff writes into the canonical design doc.

verdict.reason: The finding's evidence checks out verbatim. docs/design/cli.md:839-845 states "Every command that renders a *structured result* routes it through `output()`" and enumerates exceptions as only the prose acknowledgements (login/logout/ctx switch) and the export file writers. But docs/notes/slides `import` emit structured JSON results directly: packages/cli/src/docs/import.ts:167 and :215, packages/cli/src/notes/import.ts:163 and :217, packages/cli/src/slides/import.ts:197-198 and :258-259 all call io.stdout(JSON.stringify(...)). A repo-wide grep for `output(`/`outputError(` lists 14 files and none of these three modules. The command wiring confirms `--format` is never read for import: packages/cli/src/commands/docs.ts:346-372 registers `import <file>` and never calls parseOutputFormat, unlike the sibling actions at docs.ts:77,101,121,140,159. Since output() is the only path that honours json|table|csv|yaml and raises InvalidFormatError (packages/cli/src/output/formatter.ts:45-50,80-82), `docs import --format table` silently emits JSON and an invalid --format is not rejected, contradicting both the §8.1 sentence and the INVALID_FORMAT contract at cli.md:855-864. Import results are neither prose acknowledgements nor document bodies, so no documented exception covers them and no guard elsewhere makes the doc claim true. This is a design-doc-discipline / spec-conformance defect in the canonical doc the diff edits — in-lane and major in kind.

finding.summary: Bundles a breaking CLI↔backend protocol coupling into a PR whose issue (#635) is about `status`/`ctx list` output formatting
finding.evidence: `login.ts` now always sends `&nonce=` and `startCallbackServer` refuses any callback whose `state` does not match, so a published `@wafflebase/cli` (independently versioned npm package, package.json:2-3) at this version can no longer complete login against any backend older than this commit — it refuses its own genuine redirect and fails after the timeout. This hard version coupling is acknowledged in docs/design/rest-api.md ("Echoing the nonce is a backend contract") and cli.md:~200, but it is a login-protocol change with a user-visible compatibility break landing in an issue scoped to routing `status`/`ctx list` through `output()` (docs/tasks/active/20260806-cli-status-ctx-structured-output-todo.md:1-41). No negotiation/opt-out (e.g. accept-but-warn on a legacy server) is offered, only a diagnostic message.

verdict.reason: The finding is accurate on every checkable point. login.ts:34,40 always mints and sends `&nonce=`, with no opt-out; startCallbackServer (228-288) refuses any callback whose `state` does not match (280-288) and never settles the wait, so against a backend that does not echo `state` the genuine redirect is refused and login fails at the 30s timeout (178, 335-341) with only a diagnostic string (REFUSAL.noState, 190-194). The backend counterpart exists (github-auth.guard.ts:36-41), and docs/design/rest-api.md:352-356 explicitly calls echoing the nonce a "backend contract" whose absence means "the server is likely older than this CLI" — the coupling is acknowledged, not mitigated. packages/cli/package.json:2-15 confirms @wafflebase/cli is an independently published npm package, so CLI/backend version skew is reachable in practice. The originating issue (docs/tasks/active/20260806-cli-status-ctx-structured-output-todo.md:1-41) is scoped entirely to routing `status`/`ctx list` through `output()`; the OAuth nonce appears only as a later review addition (118-120, 132-136), and the doc itself concedes the scope-creep finding is "accurate as a description" (155-158), declining it only on process grounds. No refutation ground applies: the code is present as described, nothing guards it, and unrequested scope creep plus approach/compat mismatch is squarely within the design-fit lens's major band.

finding.summary: Backend CLI-auth contract changed (new `nonce` query param, `state` echoed on the loopback redirect) but rest-api.md §7 "CLI Auth Endpoints" — the doc cli.md explicitly delegates the backend surface to — still documents `GET /auth/github?mode=cli&port=<port>` and a redirect of `http://127.0.0.1:<port>/callback?code=<auth-code>` with no nonce. The risk table row "OAuth state forgery (CSRF)" (line 367) is likewise unchanged despite this being the mitigation for a newly-described login-CSRF risk. cli.md §Login flow says "CSRF and port-validation details live in rest-api.md 'CLI Auth …'", so the canonical backend doc is now stale/contradictory.
finding.evidence: rest-api.md:334-342 unchanged: "redirects to `http://127.0.0.1:<port>/callback?code=<auth-code>`"; diff changes auth.controller.ts to append `&state=<nonce>` and github-auth.guard.ts to accept `?nonce=`.

verdict.reason: The claim that rest-api.md §7 is stale is false in the working tree. docs/design/rest-api.md:334-343 documents the new `nonce` query parameter (`GET /auth/github?mode=cli&port=<port>&nonce=<hex>`), its `[0-9a-f]{32,128}` validation, and its storage against the OAuth state token — matching github-auth.guard.ts:17,39. docs/design/rest-api.md:344-350 documents the loopback redirect as `http://127.0.0.1:<port>/callback?code=<auth-code>&state=<nonce>`, including that the `state` fragment is the CLI's echoed nonce and is omitted when none was carried — matching auth.controller.ts:127-135. Lines 352-357 document the backend/CLI version contract. The risk table also gained a new row at docs/design/rest-api.md:383, "Login CSRF on the CLI loopback callback", describing precisely the nonce-echo mitigation the reviewer says is undocumented; the pre-existing "OAuth state forgery (CSRF)" row has shifted from 367 to 382, which is itself evidence the section was edited and correctly stays scoped to the distinct backend-to-GitHub state token risk. The reviewer's quoted evidence ("rest-api.md:334-342 unchanged ... with no nonce") does not exist in the repository, so cli.md's delegation to rest-api.md resolves to accurate, current content.

finding.summary: Scope creep beyond the originating issue. docs/tasks/active/20260806-cli-status-ctx-structured-output-todo.md (#635) scopes this work to routing `status`/`ctx list` through `output()` and validating `--format`; the diff additionally lands a cross-package OAuth protocol change (per-attempt nonce in `cli-auth.store`, guard, callback redirect, loopback server hardening), a CSV formula-injection transform, and a `cells batch` parse restructure. Each is a separable change with its own risk surface (the OAuth one even introduces a backend/CLI version coupling), bundled into an output-formatting PR.
finding.evidence: todo.md "Review round 2" checklist items lines 116-122 add CSV neutralization, OAuth nonce, and cells-batch parsing to an issue whose Approach (lines 19-41) covers only formatter/status/ctx/schema/docs.

verdict.reason: The code the finding points at is genuinely present (login.ts nonce/loopback hardening, cli-auth.store/github-auth.guard, csv.ts neutralizer), and the diff is indeed larger than #635's Approach. But the finding's operative claim — *unrequested* scope creep — is refuted by the repository's own canonical task record: docs/tasks/active/20260806-cli-status-ctx-structured-output-todo.md:106 heads the exact block the finding cites (lines 116-122) as "Review round 2 (panel changes-requested)", i.e. the CSV neutralization, OAuth nonce and cells-batch restructure are remediation this same panel required on this PR; lines 148-158 record that this identical finding was raised in round 5 and that reverting would re-open round 2. The added scope also satisfies this lens's actual gate: design-doc discipline is met, not violated — docs/design/rest-api.md:334-356 documents the `nonce` param, the echoed `state` and the backend/CLI version coupling, and lines 382-384 add the loopback-CSRF risk row, all folded into the canonical subsystem doc rather than a parallel file. No stated Non-Goal is exceeded (docs/design/cli.md:55-70 lists account switching, device flow, token encryption, block-level Docs writes, slicing, server-side rendering, separate binary — none implicated), no acceptance criterion of #635 is unmet, and nothing duplicates an existing module. What is left is "these belonged in separate PRs", a process/taste preference that the rubric classes as minor and that never blocks — and which is not actionable here since unbundling means dropping an earlier round's mandated work.

finding.summary: The CSV formula-neutralization transform is applied inside `formatCsv`, which is also the writer for the machine data-export path `sheets export <doc-id> <file> --file-format csv` (sheets-export.ts:46). Exported cell `formula` values (`=SUM(B2:B10)`) and `-`/`+`-prefixed content now gain a leading `'`, corrupting the import→analyze→export round trip the repo advertises (skills/recipe-csv-pipeline.md, skills/sheets-import-export.md) since `sheets import`/csv-parse will read the quoted text back as a literal. The new cli.md §8.1 paragraph only scopes the behavior to `--format csv`, so the export path's change is undocumented. A display-safety escape belongs at the human-rendering layer, not on the shared serializer used for data interchange.
finding.evidence: packages/cli/src/commands/sheets-export.ts:46 `const formatted = fmt === 'csv' ? formatCsv(res.data) : formatJson(res.data);`; skills/sheets-read-cells.md:44 shows cells carrying `"formula": "=SUM(B2:B10)"`.

verdict.reason: The finding asserts that formula neutralization is applied unconditionally inside formatCsv and therefore reaches the `sheets export --file-format csv` data-interchange path, corrupting the import→export round trip, and that only `--format csv` is documented. All three claims are contradicted by the working tree. (1) packages/cli/src/output/csv.ts:40-53 defines `CsvOptions` with a REQUIRED, non-defaulted `neutralizeFormulas: boolean`, and csv.ts:74 applies `neutralizeFormula` only when that flag is true — it is not an unconditional transform on the shared serializer. (2) The exact evidence line the reviewer quotes for sheets-export.ts:46 (`const formatted = fmt === 'csv' ? formatCsv(res.data) : formatJson(res.data);`) does not exist; sheets-export.ts:50-53 reads `formatCsv(res.data, { neutralizeFormulas: false })`, preceded by a comment (lines 46-49) explaining that the file is the input of `sheets import` and that an exported `=SUM(B2:B100)` must come back as that formula. So exported `formula` values are written verbatim and no round-trip corruption occurs. The only opt-in caller is the human render path, packages/cli/src/output/formatter.ts:58-61. (3) The claim that the export path is undocumented fails: docs/design/cli.md:875-883 explicitly documents it — "Neutralization belongs to this render path only. `sheets export <doc> out.csv` writes a data file that `sheets import` reads back (skills/recipe-csv-pipeline.md), so it serializes verbatim", and explains that `formatCsv` takes an explicit flag rather than defaulting. The design remedy the finding demands (escape at the rendering layer, not the interchange serializer) is exactly what is implemented, so there is no spec-conformance or design-fit violation. Ground: not-present.

finding.summary: The nonce round trip is introduced as a hard backend/CLI compatibility break with no graceful degradation: a new CLI pointed at a server that does not echo `state` will 403 its own genuine redirect and hang until the 30s timeout, with no actionable error. The doc records the coupling ("a CLI at this version or later needs a backend at this version or later") but the change offers no fallback, feature negotiation, or diagnostic for self-hosted/older deployments — a notable approach-fit decision for a change whose stated issue is output formatting.
finding.evidence: cli.md new paragraph: "The nonce round trip is a backend contract: the loopback redirect echoes it, so a CLI at this version or later needs a backend at this version or later."; login.ts rejects a state-less code with 403 and never settles the wait.

verdict.reason: The finding's blocking premise — "no graceful degradation… no actionable error… no diagnostic" for a new CLI against an old backend — is not present as described. docs/design/cli.md:210-218 is a paragraph dedicated to exactly this scenario, stating that a refusal must not be silent because "a CLI pointed at an older backend refuses its own genuine redirect and hangs for the full 30 seconds with nothing to act on," and requiring every refusal to name its cause on stderr, in the browser tab, and in the timeout error, distinguishing the no-`state` (old server) case. The code implements this: login.ts:189-203 defines REFUSAL.noState whose text is the actionable message ("the server is likely older than this CLI — update the server, or use a CLI matching it"); login.ts:240-249 emits it to stderr immediately and as the 403 body; login.ts:279-288 picks that specific reason when `state === null`; login.ts:206-209 and 335-341 repeat it in the timeout rejection. test/login.test.ts:108-121 asserts the timeout error matches /no `state`/ and /older than this CLI/. Only the sub-claim "rejects a state-less code with 403 and never settles the wait" is accurate, and that is the deliberate anti-CSRF design (a forged hit must not consume the wait) — accompanied by the diagnostic the finding says is missing. The residual "no automatic fallback/negotiation" cannot block under the design-fit rubric: silently accepting a state-less code would reinstate the login-CSRF the change closes, no acceptance criterion or documented Non-Goal is cited, and the coupling is recorded in the canonical cli.md/rest-api.md docs rather than a parallel doc.
